description: Pinned results of the DynamicUSP solver for the dynamic_usp scheduler type. The numbers of the sections sample_weight, tier_time_factors, plans and table_variants come from an offline run of the upstream solver at commit 1ff97a4ae0beb5e088fadb9e112265bdd194b24d with its own profile and calibration table; they are solver output, not a measurement. The runtime scheduler must reproduce them. The sections runtime_sequence_cap and runtime_h100_plans are not upstream output: they pin the runtime scheduler's own results, under its per-group sequence cap and for the measured H100 calibration, except the 'upstream' entries of two runtime_sequence_cap cases

sample_weight.description: weights.empirical_joint_weight(tokens) = max(1, A * (tokens * tokens / 1e10) + B * (tokens / 1e5) + C). 'default' uses the constants of weights.py; 'refit' and 'floor' are the same function with the module constants replaced. Compare with ==

tier_time_factors.description: gbs.config.tier_time_factors_from_profile(USPCalibV1Profile(), cp_sizes, reference_tokens): group time of the reference sample alone, times the group size, relative to the smallest size

plans.description: solve_gbs(problem, GbsConfig(max_seqlen_per_dp_cp_rank=tokens_per_rank, objective=PipelineCostModel(USPCalibV1Profile(), pipeline_parallel=1, ...).objective(), keep_candidate_layouts=True, ...)) with Sample.routing_weight = empirical_joint_weight(tokens), attention_heads=24, ulysses_degree=8. 'solver' is the section of the coefficient file and 'options' the Python solver options that give the runtime the same configuration. Every candidate count is listed: 'objective_ms' is upstream's step time, which leaves out the constant global.C_global_clean_ms of the table (the runtime adds it), and 'layout' is [[[first rank, group size, [sample index, ...]], ...] per microbatch] in execution order. The chosen candidate has the lowest objective

runtime_sequence_cap.description: NOT upstream numbers: these are the runtime scheduler's own results, pinned as a regression. Upstream has no limit on the sequences of a group, so under the runtime's cap its count window can hold no layout. The runtime adds ceil(samples / sequences one microbatch holds) to the count lower bound. A raised bound inside upstream's window skips the counts below it and keeps the last count of that window; a raised bound past that window starts a full window. When every count of the window is rejected for capacity, the runtime goes on past the window to the first count with a layout and scores a full window from there. It tries at most 16 counts past the window (4 x candidate_count) to find one. 'candidate_trail' lists every count tried, with 'ok' or the rejection; 'predicted_ms' includes the constant global.C_global_clean_ms. Original profile; every case gives its DPxCP ('world_size'), CP sizes and tokens per rank; 'options' are Python options of the solver. The two bound_inside_upstream_window cases also carry upstream output: there the runtime's plan is upstream's plan

cases.name: bound_inside_upstream_window
cases.note: DPxCP 16 with CP 8 only, default options: the sequence term raises the lower bound from 3 to 4 (414 samples, 128 sequences per microbatch), inside upstream's window, counts 3 to 6. Upstream rejects count 3 and has layouts at 4, 5 and 6 with at most 64 sequences per group. The runtime skips count 3 and ends its window where upstream's ends: it scores the same three counts and plans the same four microbatches. Count 7, which a window of four counts from the raised bound would hold, is predicted faster and is not tried. 'upstream' is solver output in the format of 'plans'

cases.name: bound_inside_upstream_window_two_counts
cases.note: DPxCP 32 with CP 8 only and the Python options outlier_threshold 2.0 and candidate_count 2: the sequence term raises the lower bound from 1 to 2 (267 samples, 256 sequences per microbatch), inside upstream's window, counts 1 and 2. Upstream rejects count 1 and plans count 2, with at most 64 sequences per group. The runtime tries count 2 only and plans it. Count 3, which a window of two counts from the raised bound would hold, is predicted faster and is not tried. 'upstream' is solver output in the format of 'plans'

runtime_h100_plans.description: NOT upstream numbers: plans of the runtime scheduler for the packaged H100 calibration (qwen3_h100_p2p), pinned as a regression from the scheduler as it was before it read solver coefficients (Stage 1 weight A, B, C, time-balance factors, the sequence cap in the count lower bound). With the default of 64 sequences per group none of that moves a plan of this calibration, which keeps its own Stage 1 weight. DPxCP 32, CP sizes 1/2/4/8, 4096 tokens per rank, EP 8, no incumbent. 'predicted_ms' is the step time of the calibration; 'layout' as in 'plans'

cases.note: 256 lengths drawn log-uniformly between 64 and 16384 tokens

pipeline_schedule.description: objectives.pipeline.interleaved_plan(microbatches, stages, virtual_stages): the operations of the interleaved schedule. 'orders' lists, per pipeline stage, the order of its operations: F or B, the microbatch and, with virtual stages, '.' and the chunk. 'digests' pins the whole plan, its order, every predecessor and every has-previous flag, for the eight counts stages, 2 x stages, ... 8 x stages of each (stages, virtual_stages): sha256 of the JSON text, without spaces, of [[[[direction, microbatch, chunk, stage], predecessor or null, has_previous], ...] per count]. 'operations' is the number of plan entries, 2 x microbatches x stages x virtual_stages

pipeline_step_time.description: PipelineCostModel(USPCalibV1Profile(), pipeline_parallel=stages, virtual_stages=virtual_stages, per_mb_overhead_ms=...).step_time_from_matrices on given group times: the replay of the interleaved schedule with group lock-step (objectives.pipeline.simulate) plus the overhead per microbatch. 'rows' lists per microbatch its groups as [first rank, ranks, forward ms, backward ms] of the whole model; every rank of a group carries the group's times. 'lock_step_toy': two ranks, group totals 150/100, 100 (both ranks one group), 100/150, 100/100 with a forward share of 1/3.9; 'without_lock_step_ms' is the same replay with independent ranks (coupled=False) and shows that the toy depends on the lock-step. 'uniform': identical microbatches of one group of eight ranks, 30 ms forward and 70 ms backward, next to uniform_makespan(100, microbatches, stages, virtual_stages). 'cases': random layouts on eight ranks. Compare step_ms with ==

pipeline_group_times.description: PipelineCostModel(USPCalibV1Profile(), compute_fwd_share=..., comm_fwd_share=...).group_time of one group: forward_ms = compute_ms * compute_fwd_share + (a2a_ms + ring_ms) * comm_fwd_share and backward_ms = compute_ms * (1 - compute_fwd_share) + (a2a_ms + ring_ms) * (1 - comm_fwd_share), with compute_ms, a2a_ms and ring_ms of USPCalibV1Profile.evaluate_group. The first shares are the defaults, 1/3.9 and 0.5

pipeline_plans.description: solve_gbs(problem, GbsConfig(max_seqlen_per_dp_cp_rank=tokens_per_rank, pp_multiple=pipeline_parallel, objective=PipelineCostModel(USPCalibV1Profile(), pipeline_parallel=pipeline_parallel, virtual_stages=virtual_stages, ...).objective(), keep_candidate_layouts=True, ...)) with the samples and the topology of 'plans'. 'solver' and 'options' are read as in 'plans'. 'count_lower_bound' is compute_bounds(...).lower; the first count is that bound rounded up to a multiple of pipeline_parallel and the next counts follow in steps of it, none above the number of samples. Candidates, scores and layouts as in 'plans': 'objective_ms' leaves out global.C_global_clean_ms, which the runtime adds once

runtime_pipeline.description: NOT upstream output of solve_gbs: the runtime scheduler's own rules at more than one pipeline stage, pinned as a regression; every count is a multiple of pipeline_parallel. Original profile. The two search_past_the_window cases: upstream's window is rejected for capacity (upstream_error); the runtime goes on, from one multiple to the next and over at most 4 x candidate_count of them, to the first count with a layout and lays out candidate_count multiples from it. Their 'candidates' are upstream's allocator, heavy-middle order and objective called on each of these counts, in the format of 'pipeline_plans' (objective_ms without global.C_global_clean_ms). The sequence_bound cases and the capacity fallback have no upstream counterpart: 'candidate_trail', 'predicted_ms' (with the constant) and the 'layout' of the fallback are the runtime's own results; 'max_group_sequences' is the cap on the sequences of a group

cases.note: DPxCP 8, one group of 8 ranks per microbatch, two pipeline stages. 24 samples of 18016 tokens, one per group, and 8 short ones: the window 14, 16, 18, 20 and count 22 are rejected for capacity; 24 is the first count with a layout and four counts are laid out from it
